correctness.rationale: The proof first gives the exact exponent characterization of D(n)=kn. For the leading support r=k it reduces log n to an additive sum of prime weights p log p. PNT gives B(L)~L/(log L)^2; regular variation yields convergence of scaled prime-weight counting measures to Lebesgue measure, so the k-fold simplex contributes 1/k!, with another 1/k! from unordered distinct primes. Repeated primes and all r<k compositions are lower order. The included finite checker independently validates the structural equivalence on a finite range.

value.rationale: The level sets of the arithmetic logarithmic derivative are a natural extension of the classical fixed-point equation. The theorem gives an exact leading constant for every fixed integral level and a structural concentration phenomenon: almost all solutions use the maximal possible number k of prime supports. This is an infinite distribution law rather than a finite census or parameter substitution.
